recipes.name: Stuffed Shells
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon salt, or more to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook until tender yet firm to the bite, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain.
While the pasta is cooking, mix ricotta cheese, 1/2 of the mozzarella cheese, 1/2 of the Parmesan cheese, eggs, parsley, salt, and pepper in a large bowl until well combined.
Combine pasta sauce and mushrooms in a medium bowl. Add remaining mozzarella and Parmesan cheeses; stir until well combined.
Stuff shells with ricotta mixture and place in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Pour pasta sauce mixture over the shells.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are bubbly and the shells are slightly set, 35 to 60 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Stuffed Shells
raw_recipe.description: Stuffed shells filled with 3 types of cheese are topped with a savory tomato sauce in this family-friendly pasta dish that'll have you coming back for more!

review.reviewBody: This is the third time i've made this and I love it. I discovered if I make the filling first and put it in the fridge for a while while preping my other items, it becomes firmer and SO much easier and neater to stuff the shells.

My family loves this recipe! My 3 year old eats shell after shell!! We're not a mushroom family, so I leave those out. I scoop the filling into a big ziploc bag, close the top up, make a small cut in one of the bottom corners and squeeze into the shells - no mess! I also divide this recipe into two 9x13 pans. We eat one and the other goes into the freezer for later. Freezes really well!

Restaurant quality! Believe it or not, I was able to reduce the fat, and it still came out delicious. I bought lowfat ricotta cheese, used only 3/4 cup mozzarella + 1/2 cup parmesan in the filling (added 1/4 tsp. salt and 1/4 tsp pepper, and would do that again), and left off the cheese in the sauce, just sprinkling a bit of parmesan after baking so it looked pretty. It made two 13x9x2 pans, and I wish I had used 2 jars of sauce instead of 1. The sauce dried out after baking, so next time, I will cover with aluminum foil first, and remove it the last 10 minutes or so. Thanks so much for the recipe - will definitely be making it again!

This was delicious! I did follow the advice of a lot of people and added a little spinach, garlic, oregano and basil to the cheese filling. Also added another 1/2 jar of sauce to the bottom of the pans.
I split the dish into 2 8x8's so I could freeze one for another meal.

I omitted the mushrooms and all of the salt. And I used my own homemade bolognese sauce. I doubled the filling recipe, and made 2 and a half pans (the disposable foil lasagna pans). I brought 2 to a party, and froze the half pan for my family. Rave reviews!

I decided to use cottage cheese in place of ricotta as I had some on hand and cottage cheese is often used in place of the more expensive ricotta. I only had a 24-oz carton of cottage cheese so I reduced the other ingredients accordingly. I also did not cook the shells ahead of time. I gently filled the "raw" shells with a teaspoon. For the shells that were too tightly curled to fill, I put them in an 8 X 8 pan (as my 11 X 7 pan was filled already with the stuffed shells) and spooned the filling over them. I spooned the sauce (I had homemade sauce) over both pans, covered tightly with aluminum foil and baked for 90 minutes. The shells cooked in the steam. I think the salt could be cut in half or even eliminated. I think it's strange to mix the cheeses with the sauce. I think it would have been better to spoon the sauce over the shells and then sprinkle the cheese on top. 

The taste was OK-it was kind of bland. I am surprised the recipe doesn't call for oregano or some other spices/herbs commonly used in Italian dishes. This recipe didn't "wow" me so I'll keep searching.

Will definitely make again. I used double the amount of Ragu sauce and added a pound of ground Italian sausage. We don’t like mushrooms. Some found the dish to be a bit salty, but we chalked it up to the Ragu and I’ll just not add the 2 teaspoons of salt next time. Hubs doesn’t like straight ricotta, so I did half ricotta, half whole milk cottage cheese. The 12 oz of pasta shells is about 35 stuffed shells; I packed my shells and had about 5 left over. I think it will make 2 9x13 pans, especially with the meat sauce. This is a hearty and very forgiving recipe.

Perfect! The only thing I did different was pour spaghetti sauce over the stuffed shells, then sprinkle the mozzarella and then the parm. No need to put spaghetti sauce on the bottom of the pan. In my opinion, it was a little too salty. Next time, I will only use 1 tsp of salt instead of 2. It yielded a tray and a half. So, I only cooked the amount I was going to cook that night and put the rest of the uncooked shells in the fridge for tomorrow's dinner. This way, it would be fresh tasting as oppose to reheating left-overs. Also, I pre-heated the oven AFTER I started filling the shells. They were ready in 30 minutes. Thanks!

Used only 1 tsp. salt and fresh parsley. Needed a 10x14 dish since you're using a full box of shells but there were still a few that couldn't fit in. Added a little sauce on the bottom before placing shells in, but felt a half cup of water would keep it from getting dry while cooking. Used a large jar of Prego sauce. Did Not top with mushrooms.

Too spicy for my wife. Next time I will only use a fraction of the black pepper.

I also added frozen chopped spinach, chopped onions - sautéed, and chopped can of mushroom stems and pieces, to the stuffing mixture.

Very good, and would probably consider adding some pesto to the sauce next time.

This was good. I put the filling mixture in a ziploc bag and cut the tip (like a pastry filler) and that cut down on the mess. For my sauce, I included ground turkey breast so that the meal was a little heartier. I also cut back on the cheese so that it would be healthier. I baked it covered for 30 minutes and uncovered for the rest.
I made this for a potluck and everyone loved it! To make the stuffing part a little easier, I used a medium cookie scoop. It put just the right amount of filling in each shell.
It tastes really good but not sure why so watery on the bottom of the dish
Easy to make, very tasty. Interesting with the cheeses mixed into the sauce.
Good. Think I'll stick with my old recipe though. Didn't use mushrooms or mix mozzarella in the sauce.
Great recipie
I add shredded cooked spinach. Absolutely delicious!!!
100% great. Give it a try and you will not be disappointed.
Easy work for wonderful result. Eats like a restaurant without sweating like a chef😉

Pre made the stuffing mix. Later that day...Assembled the shells, covered and refrigerated to made for dinner the following night. Used extra sauce but otherwise followed the recipe as written. Was delicious! As far as shell recipes go, this was relatively easy. Will definitely make again.
